meta.title: Tax planning strategies and their limits
meta.summary: The three basic planning strategies: timing, income shifting and conversion, how the time value of money drives them, and the doctrines that stop plans going too far.

videos.title: Three ways to plan
videos.take: Timing, income shifting and conversion are the three basic tax planning strategies

scenes.say: Tax planning isn't about tricks. Almost every legitimate strategy is one of three moves. Here they are.

scenes.heading: Three basic strategies
items: Timing: when income and deductions land
Income shifting: who reports the income
Conversion: what kind of income it is
scenes.say: Timing changes when income or deductions are recognized. Income shifting moves income to a taxpayer in a lower bracket. Conversion changes the type of income, for example from ordinary income to a capital gain taxed at a lower rate.
The goal is to maximize after-tax wealth, not to minimize tax. Turning down a raise would cut your tax bill, but it would make you poorer.

scenes.heading: Good planning considers
items: Every party to the deal
Every tax: federal, state, payroll
Every cost, tax and non-tax
scenes.say: Good planning looks at every party to a transaction, every tax that applies, and every cost, including the non-tax ones like lost flexibility or legal fees.

scenes.heading: Which strategy?
scenes.say: Paying a property tax bill in December instead of January is timing. Paying fifteen-year-old Leo to help in Nora's business shifts income to him. Holding shares for more than a year converts a short-term gain into a lower-taxed long-term gain.

scenes.q: Jake chooses a tax-exempt municipal bond over a taxable bond. Which strategy is this?
scenes.say: Quick check. Jake chooses a tax-exempt municipal bond over a taxable bond. Which strategy is it? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's C, conversion. He changes the type of income, from taxable interest to tax-exempt interest.

videos.title: Timing and the time value of money
videos.take: A deduction is worth more the sooner you take it, because of the time value of money

scenes.say: A dollar of tax saved today is worth more than a dollar saved next year. That simple fact drives timing strategies.

sub: What a future amount is worth today,
scenes.say: Present value is what a future amount is worth today. At a six percent return, a dollar received next year is worth about ninety-four cents now.

scenes.heading: A $10,000 deduction, 24% bracket, 6% rate
rows: Tax saved if deducted this year
Tax saved next year, in today's dollars
scenes.say: Erik, Jake's brother, is in the twenty-four percent bracket. A ten thousand dollar deduction saves him $2,400. Taken this year, that's $2,400 today. Taken next year, it's worth only $2,264 today. Accelerating is worth $136.

scenes.heading: So, when rates stay the same
items: Accelerate deductions into this year
Defer income into next year
scenes.say: So, when tax rates stay the same, accelerate deductions and defer income. Both keep money in your hands longer.
Deferring tax is like an interest-free loan from the government. That's why retirement accounts, which defer tax for decades, are so valuable.

scenes.q: Erik can deduct $5,000 in December or January. Same 24% rate both years. When should he?
scenes.say: Quick check. Erik can deduct five thousand dollars in December or January, with the same twenty-four percent rate both years. When should he? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's A, December. The $1,200 tax saving arrives a year sooner, so it's worth more.

videos.title: When rates change
videos.take: If your rate will rise, reverse the rule: accelerate income and defer deductions

scenes.say: Accelerate deductions and defer income. That rule flips when your tax rate is about to change.

scenes.heading: $10,000 deduction, rate rising from 24% to 32%
rows: Next year's saving in today's dollars
scenes.say: Suppose Erik expects a promotion that moves him from twenty-four to thirty-two percent next year. Deducting now saves $2,400. Waiting saves $3,200, worth $3,019 today. Deferring the deduction wins by $619.

scenes.heading: The rule depends on rates
scenes.say: So if rates are flat or falling, accelerate deductions and defer income. If rates are rising enough, do the opposite: defer deductions and accelerate income.

scenes.heading: Rates change when
items: Income jumps or drops: a new job, retirement
Filing status changes: marriage, divorce
Congress changes the law
scenes.say: Your rate changes when your income jumps or drops, when your filing status changes, or when Congress changes the law, as it did in 2017 and again in 2025.
Don't apply the rule blindly. Compare the after-tax present value of each option.

scenes.q: Nora expects a much lower rate next year while she cuts back work. When should she take a $3,000 bonus from a client?
scenes.say: Quick check. Nora expects a much lower rate next year while she cuts back on work. When should she take a three thousand dollar payment from a client? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B, next year. Deferring income into a lower-rate year saves tax and delays it.

videos.title: Shifting income within the family
videos.take: Shift income to lower-bracket family members through real work, within the kiddie tax rules

scenes.say: Same income, lower bracket. Shifting income to a family member can save tax, if it's done properly.

scenes.heading: Nora pays Leo $8,000 for real work
rows: Leo's tax: standard deduction covers it
scenes.say: Fifteen-year-old Leo edits photos for Nora's business. She pays him $8,000, a fair wage for the work. Nora deducts it, saving about $960 of income tax and $1,130 of self-employment tax. Leo's standard deduction covers his wages, so he pays nothing.
It only works if the work is real and the pay is reasonable. A child under eighteen working for a parent's sole proprietorship also owes no Social Security or Medicare tax.

sub: is taxed at the parents' rate
scenes.say: Shifting investment income is harder. Under the kiddie tax, a child's unearned income over $2,700 in 2026 is taxed at the parents' rate. It applies to children under nineteen, and full-time students under twenty-four.

sub: to the person who earned it
scenes.say: And you can't simply assign your paycheck to your child. Income is taxed to whoever earns it. The Supreme Court said in 1930 that the fruit can't be attributed to a different tree from the one on which it grew.

scenes.q: Ava, 8, has $5,000 of dividends in 2026. How much is taxed at her parents' rate?
scenes.say: Quick check. Eight-year-old Ava has five thousand dollars of dividends. How much is taxed at her parents' rate? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's C. Unearned income above $2,700 is taxed at the parents' rate: 5,000 minus 2,700 is $2,300.

videos.title: Conversion
videos.take: Converting ordinary income into capital gains or tax-exempt income lowers the rate applied

scenes.say: Not all income is taxed alike. Conversion changes the character of income to reach a lower rate.

scenes.heading: Same dollars, different rates
scenes.say: Wages and interest are ordinary income, taxed at ten to thirty-seven percent. Long-term capital gains and qualified dividends get zero, fifteen or twenty percent. Municipal bond interest is tax-exempt.

scenes.heading: Erik sells shares at a $10,000 gain
scenes.say: Erik has a ten thousand dollar gain on shares. Sell after eleven months, and it's a short-term gain taxed at his twenty-four percent rate: $2,400. Wait until he's held them more than a year, and it's taxed at fifteen percent: $1,500.

scenes.heading: Watch the non-tax costs
items: Market risk while you wait
Lower pre-tax returns on tax-exempt bonds
Less diversification
scenes.say: But conversion has costs. While Erik waits, the share price could fall. Tax-exempt bonds pay lower pre-tax yields. A good plan weighs these against the tax saved.
So the three strategies answer three questions: when is income taxed, who is taxed on it, and what kind of income is it.

scenes.q: Which change converts income to a lower rate?
opts: Taking a bonus in January instead of December
scenes.say: Quick check. Which change converts income to a lower rate? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. Holding the stock over a year turns a short-term gain into a long-term capital gain. The others are timing or shifting.

videos.title: Where planning stops
videos.take: Business purpose, step transaction and substance over form limit planning; evasion is a crime

scenes.say: Tax planning has limits. Here are the doctrines courts use to strike down plans that go too far.

sub: is taxed when it was available
scenes.say: First, constructive receipt. A cash-method taxpayer can't defer income by refusing to pick up a check. If the money was available to you without restriction, it's taxed when it was available.

scenes.heading: Three judicial doctrines
items: Business purpose: a deal needs a non-tax reason
Step transaction: linked steps are taxed as one
Substance over form: the economics decide
scenes.say: Courts also apply three doctrines. A transaction must have a business purpose beyond saving tax. Steps that only make sense together are collapsed into one. And the substance of a deal, not its legal form, decides how it's taxed.

scenes.heading: Avoidance or evasion?
rows: Waiting a year for the lower rate
scenes.say: Tax avoidance, using the law to reduce tax, is legal. Tax evasion, hiding income or inventing deductions, is a crime, punishable by fines and prison.

scenes.big: Would it make sense without the tax?
scenes.say: A useful test: would the transaction make sense if there were no tax? If not, expect the IRS to challenge it.

scenes.q: On December 30 Nora's client hands her a $2,000 check. She holds it and deposits it in January. When is it income?
scenes.say: Quick check. On December thirtieth a client hands Nora a two thousand dollar check. She deposits it in January. When is it income? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's A, December. She received it and could have deposited it. Holding the check doesn't defer the income.

warmup: Your employer offers you a $5,000 bonus on December 28 or January 3. Which do you pick, and why?
Students usually pick December (cash now). Draw out the tax angle: January defers tax a year, December is better if next year's rate will be higher. Leads to 3.2 and 3.3.
acts: Classify each as timing, shifting or conversion: (a) Roth IRA contribution, (b) gifting shares to a child in college, (c) delaying an invoice to January, (d) buying municipal bonds.
(a) Conversion (tax-free growth) and timing. (b) Shifting, subject to the kiddie tax for students under 24. (c) Timing. (d) Conversion.
A 22% taxpayer can deduct $8,000 now or in one year; the discount rate is 5%. What is the value of accelerating?
The same $8,000 deduction, but next year's rate will be 32%. Now or later?
Nora wants to pay Ava, 8, $10,000 for 'modeling' in two photos. What concerns would the IRS raise?
Reasonableness: $10,000 for two photos is not an arm's-length wage. The excess is a disguised gift; the deduction would be denied.
Erik's shares have a $6,000 gain after 10 months. He is in the 24% bracket. What does waiting 3 more months save, and what is the risk?
6,000 × (24% − 15%) = $540. Risk: the price could fall by more than $540.
A taxpayer sells land to his wholly owned corporation and has it sell to a buyer the next day. Which doctrine applies?
Step transaction (and substance over form): the steps are collapsed into a direct sale.
case: In December 2026, Nora's photography business has had a strong year and the Lindqvists are in the 22% bracket. Next year Nora plans to take six months off when the family adopts a baby, so they expect to fall into the 12% bracket. Nora is owed $6,000 by clients and has $4,000 of new equipment she could buy in December or January. Leo, 15, has been helping with editing.
Should Nora bill and collect the $6,000 before or after December 31?
Should she buy the equipment in December or January?
Is paying Leo a sensible shift? What records should she keep?

Income: defer to the 12% year (bill in late December, collect in January only if not constructively received). Equipment: accelerate the deduction into the 22% year. Paying Leo a reasonable wage for real editing work shifts income and saves SE tax; keep timesheets and pay by check. Non-tax: cash flow, client relations, whether she needs the equipment now.
exam: Explain the three basic tax planning strategies and give one example of each.

Timing (when: accelerate deductions, defer income); income shifting (who: wages to children, subject to kiddie tax and assignment-of-income limits); conversion (what kind: long-term gains, municipal interest).

A taxpayer in the 24% bracket can take a $20,000 deduction this year or next. The discount rate is 6%. Compute the present value of the tax savings in each case if (a) rates stay the same and (b) next year's rate is 35%. Advise.
outcomes: Name the three basic planning strategies
Use present value to compare timing choices
Explain why rising rates reverse the timing rule
Shift income within limits, including the kiddie tax
Convert ordinary income to lower-taxed income
Apply the judicial doctrines and tell avoidance from evasion
take: Plan for after-tax wealth, not the lowest tax
Accelerate deductions and defer income when rates hold
Reverse the rule when rates will rise
Shifting needs real work and reasonable pay
Long-term gains and tax-exempt income convert to lower rates
A plan needs a business purpose; evasion is a crime

items: Prepay property tax in December
Pay a child a wage for real work
Buy municipal bonds
Delay a client invoice to January
Hold shares longer than a year
Give shares to a grandparent in a low bracket
ex.why: Timing is when, shifting is who, conversion is what kind of income.

ex.q: A 24% taxpayer's $10,000 deduction is delayed one year. At a 6% discount rate, what is the present value of the tax saved next year?
Rates are rising from 24% to 35% next year. What should a taxpayer generally do?
ex.why: A deduction is worth more and income costs more in the high-rate year.

ex.q: A 12-year-old has $4,000 of interest income in 2026. How much is taxed at the parents' rate?
ex.why: Unearned income over $2,700 is taxed at the parents' rate: 4,000 − 2,700 = 1,300.

ex.q: A 24% taxpayer has an $8,000 gain. How much tax does holding for more than a year save if the long-term rate is 15%?
Match each doctrine to its idea.
pairs: A deal needs a non-tax reason
Linked steps are taxed as one

items: Contributing to a 401(k)
Leaving cash tips off the return
Claiming a dependent who doesn't exist
Buying municipal bonds
Timing a sale for long-term treatment
ex.why: Avoidance uses the rules; evasion breaks them.

ex.q: Under the assignment-of-income doctrine, who is taxed on Jake's salary if he directs his employer to pay it to Leo?
ex.why: Income from services is taxed to the person who earns it.
